saints.name: St. Wenceslaus
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The Christian duke of Bohemia, raised by his holy grandmother, murdered at the church door by his own brother…
biography: Born about 907, Wenceslaus -- Václav in Czech -- was the son of Duke Vratislaus of Bohemia and was reared in the faith by his grandmother St. Ludmila, who in 921 was strangled at Tetín by agents of his mother Drahomíra. As duke he governed as a Christian prince, building the rotunda of St. Vitus at Prague Castle and relieving the poor with his own hand.

His piety and his submission to the German king Henry the Fowler, who forced him to tribute in 929, made him enemies among the nobles. In 935 his brother Boleslaus invited him to Stará Boleslav for the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian, and there, at the church door on 28 September, Boleslaus's men set upon him, the brother himself striking the final blow.

Venerated from his death as a martyr, his relics were translated in 938 to St. Vitus's in Prague, and the Emperor Otto I is said to have granted him the royal title, whence the 'king' of legend and of the carol 'Good King Wenceslas'. As the martyred prince of his nation he is the patron of Bohemia and of the Czech people.
saints.knownFor: His just Christian rule and his martyrdom at his brother's hand.
